- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 88.00), model often overshoots; cap next 3 days’ forecast at +5% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward by 2–3% per day.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 85.00 and true outcome drops below 82.00 within 5 days, model overestimates; apply 3–5% downward correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows volatility, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–3% buffer for lower tail.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days: model tends to overestimate long-term mean; apply 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
